Lines 97-118 discover installed Xcodes while respecting explicit DEVELOPER_DIR; lines 150-160 bind the wrapper to the script directory and propagate a changed Xcode selection. These changes affect signed-artifact qualification (A-017, T-054), but no supported authorization bypass or adversarial runner-path prerequisite is established. Added test patches exercise rejection, SDK normalization, argument preservation and Xcode selection; tests were not executed.

scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py:82 changes the asserted build SDK to 27.2 while retaining source/tag, successful-job and immutable-artifact checks at lines 34-78. Integration must verify release callers explicitly select release mode (the script defaults to qualification), and that artifact download/inventory checks validate actual SDK provenance against this assertion rather than merely copying it. Neither callers nor artifact validators are supplied; an older resumable artifact is not established here, so no regression finding is warranted.

The documentation's changed SDK declaration at docs/operations/provider-release.md:631 matches the pin. Supplied lines 905-1126 are unchanged surrounding operational guidance, including registration bounds, immutable recovery, revocation and rollback; they do not establish new deployment or cluster authorization behavior. No direct changes to prompt encryption, keys, cache isolation (T-041), billing, fan authority or local add-on boundaries appear in this scope. Remaining material review concerns are cross-file release/qualification provenance and consistent SDK/Xcode use through signing, not evidence that runtime controls are safe.
